title: Love is not a feeling you possess; it is a field you enter.
sourceTitle: Closeness to Allah and Perfect Humanity
passage: And beneath the delightful gaze of the beloved. So we are never separate from the beloved. So, whether we are by ourself in retreat, or whether we are out with companions and in humanity in on the earth in the world. We are never separate from the beloved experiencing the delicacy of divinely human love. So, what does that mean divinely human love means the love that we don't grasp or claim for ourself, it simply means rejoicing in relationships of love rejoicing in love itself for it is the love of the beloved.
interpretation: The lesson is that love is not something we manufacture and then own. Shaykha points toward love as a reality already surrounding us â present in solitude, companionship, ordinary human relationships, and the world itself. The spiritual mistake is to grasp at love as mine: my feeling, my relationship, my spiritual achievement. The deeper move is to rejoice in love wherever it appears because it belongs to the Beloved before it belongs to us.
goldenInsight: Love becomes divine when we stop claiming it and start recognizing it.
practice: When you feel love for a person, place, teacher, child, friend, or memory, pause and say inwardly: This love is not mine to possess; it is mine to honor.

title: Remembrance is not private spirituality; it is charity to the world.
sourceTitle: Sufi Talk on Servants of Divine Love and Charity
passage: These are words of Rasulullah ï·º. Every step taken on the way to prayer, so we would say also Zikr, is pure charity to the world. So let's give that even more meaning, or go deeper into the meaning of that. That every step taken in prayer, in a state of prayer, in a state of Zikr, in a state of conscious love, is charity to the world. So our Zikr, and I'm not speaking just of the communal Zikr, our Zikr as we intone it, as we go out or as we sit in our house, is charity to the world.
interpretation: This teaching reframes spiritual practice as a form of service. Zikr is not only for the one remembering. It changes the atmosphere around the person. It becomes a contribution to the moral and spiritual climate of the world. Even a private remembrance in the house is described as charity because it adds conscious love to creation.
goldenInsight: A remembered heart gives charity even before the hands move.
practice: Before entering a meeting, family conversation, public place, or difficult task, take one breath of remembrance and offer the steadiness of that breath as charity to the space.

title: Trust is not passive optimism; it is relationship with the One who can be relied upon.
sourceTitle: On Trust and Submission in Islam
passage: The key to trust is submission. From trust, if one contemplates it and looks within and asks oneself, how do we attain trust? How do we come to that state where we can rely entirely upon Allah's promise? And Allah says, I never break my promise, which is right there, an invitation for contemplation, because we often break our promises. I mean, if we look, even during the day, if we become cognizant, how many times we say we'll do something and then we don't do it, but we are something and we are not.
interpretation: Shaykha is distinguishing real trust from vague reassurance. Trust is not everything will go the way I want. It is the gradual recognition that the Divine is reliable in a way the ego is not. Human beings break promises, change moods, forget intentions, and contradict themselves. The lesson is not to shame human weakness, but to see why the heart needs a more trustworthy ground.
goldenInsight: Trust begins when the heart stops asking the ego to be God.
practice: When anxious control appears, ask: What promise am I trying to force the world to make? What would it mean to entrust this to Allah instead?

title: Patience is the discipline that allows knowledge to ripen.
sourceTitle: Patience, Poverty, and Spiritual Knowledge in Islam
passage: So in this ayat, we have the linking of knowledge and patience. And it's interesting that Effendi would teach sometimes on that subject of knowledge and patience, and he would say that without patience, we can't really have knowledge, we can't progress in our knowing without patience. So, you know, what is patience? And so, patience, what is patience? Patience is, according to Ibn Arabi, in a very brief description of the name, it is having the power to, in that case he used to take revenge or to enact something, and not using it.
interpretation: This is a lesson about restraint as intelligence. Shaykha links patience with knowledge because knowledge is not merely information. To know spiritually, one must be able to wait, refrain, hold tension, and resist premature reaction. Patience is especially difficult when we have the power to act. The lesson is that power does not become wisdom until it can restrain itself.
goldenInsight: Patience is power that has learned not to spend itself too soon.
practice: When you feel the urge to reply, correct, punish, decide, or explain immediately, wait one full breath longer than usual. Let knowledge catch up to power.

title: Humility is not self-hatred; it is the doorway to forgiveness.
sourceTitle: Ramadan Reflections on Forgiveness and Mercy
passage: We are servants of your servants. So this is the humility, which is part of the asking for forgiveness, because if we're not humble, we can't ask for forgiveness or we won't find ourselves. And you know, there are paths where forgiveness is not included, and where it's maybe more the idea of being strong or perfect or as great as you can be. And those are ways of delusion, because our way, inshallah, is the way of safety, which is the way of humbleness and acknowledging our wrongs.
interpretation: The teaching separates humility from humiliation. Humility is not a negative self-image. It is the condition that makes repair possible. If a person must always appear strong, perfect, right, or spiritually advanced, then forgiveness becomes inaccessible because there is no room to admit harm or need.
goldenInsight: Humility is the door through which forgiveness can enter.
practice: At the end of the day, name one thing without drama: Here I was limited. Here I need mercy. Here I can return.

title: The ego separates; the heart notices separation and asks to return.
sourceTitle: Invocation and Reflection on Divine Forgiveness
passage: The dervish soul exists in conscious loving communion and community with all souls. Whenever the limited self attempts to separate from others, placing itself in opposition to others, or in competition with others, or making itself seem superior to others, the sensitive dervish heart cries out, May Allah forgive me. Whenever the limited self attempts to separate from others. So, these are all very subtle actions on the part of the limited self. And when we have become sensitive and aware, let's say more aware of ourself, we can detect these moments.
interpretation: This is a practical anatomy of ego. The ego is not only obvious arrogance. It appears whenever the self makes separation: opposition, competition, superiority, even subtle comparison. Shaykhaâs lesson is not to become paranoid about the self, but to become sensitive. The heart learns to detect the moment when it leaves communion and starts building a private throne.
goldenInsight: The ego separates quietly; the awakened heart returns quickly.
practice: When you compare yourself to someone â above or below â say inwardly: This too is separation. Bring me back into communion.

title: Service begins when another personâs suffering is allowed to come near.
sourceTitle: Tawakkul, Compassion, and Responsibility in Crisis
passage: When we feel that everything is near to us, so another suffering is near to us. And so we ask for Allah to bless all those who are suffering and to remove their suffering when Allah wills to remove their suffering. And to remove their suffering for the sake of Rasulullah, who came as the mercy to the world. And we ask for Allah to open the hearts of those who are perpetrating suffering for the sake of Rasulullah. Allah sent the Rasul to awaken the hearts and to sensitize them to the other, to each other, to make us realize our divine compassion that has been placed in us.
interpretation: The lesson is that compassion begins with nearness. The suffering of others often remains abstract because we keep it far away: as news, politics, statistics, or someone elseâs problem. Shaykha teaches that the prophetic function is to awaken sensitivity â to make the other real to the heart.
goldenInsight: Compassion begins when distance collapses.
practice: When hearing of suffering, resist the impulse to scroll past immediately. Pause long enough to let one real human being become near in your heart, then make one prayer or one concrete act.

title: Creation is generous by nature; consciousness makes the vessel shine.
sourceTitle: Blessings, Ascension, and the Salawat Reflection
passage: So, of course, this is not just limited to that moment and salat, that we are always functioning as these transmitters of this grace and mercy to others. We are always sharing it, whether we know so or not, and that's the beauty of the nature of creation. The creation by nature is generous and wise and beautiful. And so, but it becomes even more beautiful when the one who is the vessel becomes conscious, and so there is a light, the vessel becomes pure light.
interpretation: This teaching presents the human being as a transmitter. We are already participating in the circulation of grace and mercy, even unconsciously. But consciousness changes the quality of participation. Creation is already generous, wise, and beautiful; the awakened person becomes a clearer vessel of that generosity.
goldenInsight: The vessel does not create the light; it becomes clear enough to transmit it.
practice: Before an ordinary action â cooking, writing, parenting, working, driving â ask: What quality am I transmitting through this? Then choose one: mercy, steadiness, beauty, patience, generosity.

title: Community is the womb where the soul matures.
sourceTitle: Sufi Talk on Servants of Divine Love and Charity
passage: Let's give thanks for our community, because the community is the womb in which our soul matures, and we're so blessed that we can gather in community here on Zoom. We have to gather physically. And we gather in community even beyond Zoom, spiritually, we're all connected and the more we are aware and conscious of the community and orient our heart to goodness toward the community, then the more also benefit we receive from the community. The community is really where it happens. I mean, it happens in our own soul, but the community is the womb, I'd like to call it the womb of birth.
interpretation: Shaykha describes community not as a social accessory but as a spiritual organ. The soul matures in relationship. It needs the friction, mercy, correction, nourishment, and shared remembrance of others. Even when inner transformation happens in our own soul, the conditions for that transformation are communal.
goldenInsight: The soul grows in the womb of relationship.
practice: Before entering a community space, ask: Am I coming to consume, compare, hide, or contribute? Then choose one small act of orientation toward goodness.

title: Adab turns existence into a feast.
sourceTitle: Reflections on Adab, Servanthood, and Love
passage: Beloveds, after last Friday's Jummah, I felt so much was left unsaid that I wanted to speak again of Adab and maybe go into more detail on Adab. So the root meaning, or let's say one of the root meanings of Adab is the feast, a feast. So one would imagine then how to, so many reflections come from the root, you could say that Adab itself is a feast. And also that when we are in harmony, when we are in Adab, we feel that we're at a feast, Allah's feast, and together with all creation.
interpretation: Adab is often translated as manners, courtesy, or spiritual etiquette, but Shaykha opens it into something more radiant. Adab is the harmony that allows us to experience existence as a feast. When a person is in right relationship â with Allah, others, the body, the moment, and creation â life becomes received rather than consumed.
goldenInsight: Adab is how the soul learns to sit at the feast of creation.
practice: Choose one ordinary threshold â entering a room, opening a laptop, beginning a meal, joining a call â and treat it as entering a feast. Slow down, greet, receive, and participate with respect.

title: Death is woven into every moment of becoming.
sourceTitle: Reflections on Death, Love, and Spiritual Passing
passage: Every moment is a moment of passing, every moment really is a moment of what we call death and new life. There is no death without life and there is no life without death, except in the hereafter where Allah says, you will only taste, you know, these two deaths and I hope I'm not misquoting the Quran, but after that there is no death and I assume that the one death is the death that we die from the body and the second death could be the fana where before the resurrection.
interpretation: This lesson removes death from abstraction. Death is not only the final biological event; passing is happening continuously. Each moment dies into the next. Each identity, mood, plan, and certainty is being replaced. To notice this is not morbid. It makes life more truthful.
goldenInsight: Every moment teaches death; every surrender teaches new life.
practice: At the end of a day, ask: What died today? What was born? What am I being asked to release into Allah?

title: Truth is not an idea we admire; it is a way we must live.
sourceTitle: Seeking Allah's Pleasure: Love, Remembrance, Service
passage: So always turn into one's heart, and whatever one does, recognizing truth. Also, in a way you could say it's part of knowledge of the knowing, recognizing truth so truth is everywhere I mean we are in the ocean of truth, but sometimes truth speaks in a way that calls in different ways. Something you follow, or something that inspires you to learn more about seeing the truth, recognizing the truth and then ultimately immersing in the truth and becoming the truth. And then of course, part of that path is to pay very close attention to what one says to speak truthfully. How can we become truth, or even really recognize truth if we are not truthful ourselves.
interpretation: The lesson is that truth is participatory. We do not recognize truth from a distance while continuing to live falsely. The capacity to see truth depends on the willingness to speak truth, practice truth, and become truthful. Shaykha moves from recognition to immersion to becoming: truth is first noticed, then followed, then inhabited.
goldenInsight: Truth can only be recognized by the part of us willing to become truthful.
practice: Before speaking, especially when afraid of consequences, ask: Will this sentence make me more able or less able to recognize truth?

title: Begin every prayer by remembering what is worthy of praise.
sourceTitle: Seeking Help from Allah: Ya Nasir Reflection
passage: And that will also help bring Allah more present to you, to us. So in prayer, and then there's the great prayers, the prayers of the prophets, the prayers of like Imam Hussain, or the prayers of Jesus, the prayers of Moses, of Abraham, prayers of Mary. And it's good to pattern our prayer on that also too, because those prayers are prayers of praise, you know, where usually we praise Allah first. You will usually find in the prayer of the Prophet Muhammad, that he will begin with praise. So this is a wonderful form of prayer.
interpretation: The lesson is that prayer is not only asking. It begins by reordering attention. Praise reminds the heart who it is addressing before it names what it needs. Shaykha points to prophetic prayer as a pattern: praise first, request after. The soul becomes less frantic when it begins from reverence instead of demand.
goldenInsight: Praise steadies the heart before petition opens the mouth.
practice: Before asking for help, name three qualities of Allah or three gifts already present. Let request emerge from gratitude, not panic.

title: Practice is meant to make presence natural, not occasional.
sourceTitle: Preparing for Ramadan: Generosity and Night of Power
passage: Although Sheikh Nour has said, and I think this is a beautiful way of viewing it, that every night is a facet from the night of Ramadan. Every night of Ramadan is a facet from that night. And that's why every night we offer with extra prayer, or zikr, or dua, or just being present with Allah. So, we can make beautiful meditation, just sitting in our heart, feeling that we are sitting on Allah's prayer carpet, and opening our heart to receive Allah's beauty and presence and love in our hearts, and allow that to spread. So, that will be the collecting the Qur'an of our own heart.
interpretation: This lesson makes sacred time portable. Ramadan is not only a date on the calendar; each night can become a facet of its light when the heart sits in presence. Practice is the bridge between occasional inspiration and a life that naturally returns to Allah. The image of sitting on Allahâs prayer carpet makes meditation intimate, embodied, and receptive.
goldenInsight: Sacred time opens wherever the heart becomes present.
practice: At night, sit for two minutes as if your heart were on a prayer carpet. Do not perform. Receive.

title: Submission is not forced defeat; it is the ground of creation.
sourceTitle: Luminous Way of Submission and Love
passage: And even though we exercise our will on a certain level, on the deeper level we are completely, as we said, possessed and moved and directed and manifested. Really, we are manifested moment by moment. So, it's actually a beautiful entrance into a deeper level of submission and being able to submit from that place, knowing that we are already submitted. Everything in this entire creation is entirely submitted. And so, it's a beautiful entry point because the base point is the fundamental of everything, rather than coming from the top where we feel we have to have our hands tied and pushed down and forced.
interpretation: Shaykha reframes submission away from coercion. The ego imagines submission as being overpowered. But the deeper teaching is that creation is already held, moved, and manifested by Allah. Submission becomes a recognition of reality rather than a humiliating surrender to force. It is not the loss of dignity; it is alignment with the deepest structure of existence.
goldenInsight: Submission is not being pushed down; it is realizing we are already held.
practice: When resistance tightens the body, ask: Where am I already being carried? Let one place of the body soften into that support.

title: Neediness can become joy when it points back to Allah.
sourceTitle: Mevlana's Teachings on Spiritual Poverty and Praise
passage: So I would like for us to, on this day, contemplate our innate poverty and how that can give us joy because that is where Allah is in the annihilation, ultimately, of our own self so that we are even poor of ourself. We are not even constituting ourself. It is simply an illusion, but that illusion has tremendous consequences. And if we hold on to that illusion, we remain unsatisfied and breathless and we can commit great errors if we let go of that illusion and accept our poverty and trust in Allah. Accepting that goes with trust also.
interpretation: The lesson is that spiritual poverty is not deprivation; it is truthfulness about dependence. The self imagines that it is self-constituting, self-secure, and self-owned. That illusion creates breathlessness because it asks the self to carry what only Allah can carry. Joy enters when poverty becomes a release from pretending.
goldenInsight: Poverty becomes joy when the self stops pretending to be its own source.
practice: When you feel insufficient, try not to immediately cover it with performance. Say: This need is a doorway, not a defect.

title: Work against injustice without letting failure harden the heart.
sourceTitle: Reflections on Justice, Zikr, and Jummah Prayer
passage: So the Shaykh Al-Akbar says that Allah is hurt by injustice when it manifests in human beings on earth. And so that our desire to turn that and to dispel that injustice is, inshallah, the wanting to do so for Allah's sake. And he said, so Shoaib said that an indication when it's really for Allah's sake is that when we're not successful at doing it, that we are not depressed or deflated or frustrated or angry.
interpretation: This is a severe and tender teaching about justice. The desire to resist injustice can be sacred, but the ego easily attaches itself to visible success, control, and emotional victory. Shaykha offers a test: if the work is truly for Allah, failure does not destroy the worker. The heart remains available for continued service rather than collapsing into bitterness.
goldenInsight: Justice work is purified when failure does not turn the heart away from love.
practice: After an effort fails or feels too small, ask: Can I keep serving without needing this moment to prove me right?

title: Beauty hushes the intellect so the heart can receive.
sourceTitle: Contemplating Divine and Human Beauty in Islam
passage: In fact our talk today is about beauty, our khutbah, is about divine beauty and human beauty, creation beauty. I am beautiful, I am the beautiful and I love beauty. So this is such an astonishing revelation of a lot to us and because it goes directly to our heart. It doesn't, it's not something that addresses really first the intellect because in the face of beauty intellect is hushed, intellect is humbled and so when Allah says to us I am the beautiful, all of a sudden all of our pores, our senses, our faculties open and blossom to receive this astonishing and love creating statement and I love beauty.
interpretation: Shaykha teaches beauty as a mode of revelation. Beauty does not first argue with the mind; it quiets the mind. It opens the pores, the senses, and the faculties so the person can receive with the whole being. Beauty is therefore not decorative. It is a way the heart is softened into receptivity.
goldenInsight: Beauty is revelation before it becomes explanation.
practice: Spend one minute with something beautiful without analyzing it. Let the body receive before the mind names.

title: The earth hears the state we walk with.
sourceTitle: Seeking Allah's Pleasure: A Jummah Reflection
passage: And the servants of Rahman are those who walk gently on the earth. So that's a very important qualification, those who walk gently. And so if we become cognizant of how we walk on the earth and in what states, what state we are in, are we pounding the earth, are we stomping the earth, are we, you know, prancing on the earth, are we walking it with pride, are we walking it with anger? Everything that is in ourself resounds and manifests. And so that is one of the manifestations, is the vibration that our state brings to the earth.
interpretation: This lesson makes spirituality physical. Our state is not hidden inside us; it resounds through the body and enters the world through ordinary gestures. Even walking becomes a moral and spiritual expression. Gentleness is not an abstract virtue but a vibration the earth can receive from us.
goldenInsight: The body reveals the state the mouth may hide.
practice: Once a day, walk ten steps as a servant of Rahman: gently, consciously, without pounding your state into the earth.

title: Consultation includes the voices we are used to overlooking.
sourceTitle: Shura and Building a Spiritual Community
passage: And even though we might be small, numerically, but I think we are actually very strong, spiritually. And so, this vision of the community is one to adhere to, and one to practice. And then, of course, there's a community that goes beyond our immediate community, with the community of the family, where we consult each other, and where we can consult our children. We should consult our children. One of the things that I found destructive in the schooling of my children was that the school administrators never consulted the children.
interpretation: The lesson is that community wisdom expands when consultation becomes real. Shaykha moves shura from a formal ideal into family, children, and everyday structures. To consult children is to admit that those affected by a decision carry knowledge adults often miss. Spiritual community is not only leadership; it is listening.
goldenInsight: A community becomes wiser when it consults the people it could easily ignore.
practice: Before making a decision for someone, ask them one sincere question about their experience and let the answer change something.

title: The fear of others is where hypocrisy begins.
sourceTitle: Muharram Reflections on Imam Hussain and Hypocrisy
passage: So truth is the powerful dispeller of darkness. And it says when truth comes, illusion and untruth vanishes. So to be not a hypocrite is to be someone who stands in the truth, with the truth. But it entails all the other virtues, because it means one, that you really only care that Allah knows and sees, and Allah is the knower and the seer and the hearer of what's in our heart and what is the truth. Because most of us fall into hypocrisy when we're afraid of others, we're afraid of the opinion of others.
interpretation: Shaykha names fear as the doorway into hypocrisy. Hypocrisy is not only deliberate deception; it is what happens when the heart becomes more concerned with human opinion than divine seeing. Truth dispels darkness because it simplifies the audience. The soul becomes freer when it remembers who actually knows and sees.
goldenInsight: Hypocrisy begins when the opinion of others becomes louder than the gaze of Allah.
practice: When tempted to perform an image, ask: What would I say or do if I only cared that Allah knows?
